works.title: On Learning
works.note: The joy and discipline of study that open the Analects — and the conviction that any companion, good or bad, can be your teacher.

works.title: Humaneness — Ren
works.note: Ren, the central Confucian virtue: a benevolence never solitary and never far off, waiting only to be willed.

works.title: Reciprocity — the Golden Rule
works.note: The single word Confucius offered as a rule for all of life — do not do to others what you would not want done to yourself — and its positive form.

works.title: The Superior Man — Junzi
works.note: The junzi, the person of cultivated character, set against the 'mean man,' distinguished by what he seeks and where he looks for it.

works.title: On Governing
works.note: Government by virtue rather than force — the ruler who, like the pole-star, draws order to himself by the rightness of his own conduct.

works.title: The Measure of a Life
works.note: Self-examination and the long work of becoming — including the most famous self-portrait in the Analects, the stages from fifteen to seventy.
